Not on record: The business has only 2 paid orders and 1 lead on record — a welcome email implies an existing customer base or subscriber list. The owner should record: the intended recipient list or trigger event for this email (e.g., 'sent to every customer immediately after first purchase').
Not on record: No record covers the brand or business name to use in the email sign-off or header. The owner should record: the official business/brand name.
Removed "The customer's candle is on its way." — it says something about the reader's own order or booking, and nothing here knows who is reading it.
Removed "The candle is made without paraffin, unlike ordinary candles." — it compares with someone else's product, and nothing this business records about itself can establish that.
Removed "The process ensures perfect results every time." — nothing on record can support a capability claim.
Removed "The candle is made from pure soy." — Fact says 'soy-only, paraffin-free' but does not state 'pure' soy or exclude other materials..
Removed "The candle is 100% soy wax." — Fact says 'soy-only, paraffin-free' but does not explicitly state '100%' soy wax..
Removed "The business uses 100% soy wax." — Fact says 'soy-only, paraffin-free material' for the candle but does not state the business uses 100% soy wax for all products..
Removed "The candles are poured at exactly 65 degrees Celsius." — Fact states 'precise temperature process (65 celsius)' but does not state the temperature is exactly 65 degrees..

Not on record: What is the burn time of a typical or competing candle the business wants to contrast against? Record as: 'Comparable candles burn for X hours.'
Not on record: Does the business want to feature one specific candle (Lavender or Rose) as the hero product in this email, or both? Record as: 'Hero product for burn-time email is [product name].'
Removed "The candles are clean." — nothing on record can support a benefit claim.
Removed "Fragrance is added at exactly 65 degrees Celsius to ensure consistent quality." — Approved fact states fragrance is added at 65°C but does not state this is 'exactly' 65°C or that it is done 'to ensure consistent quality'.

Left out: Name the service being welcomed — anchors the email to the right treatment. — a availability claim needs a record that can establish "policy", and the one(s) cited cannot.

Not on record: Aftercare instructions for the client to follow post-treatment (e.g., how many days before washing hair, products to avoid) — owner should record these as a numbered list.
Not on record: Business name / salon name to personalise the email sign-off — owner should record the trading name.
Not on record: Booking or contact details (phone number, address, booking link) to include in the email CTA — owner should record these.
Removed "Taking care of customer's hair is the business's first priority" — nothing on record can support a capability claim.
Removed "All treatments use ammonia-free products" — Fact says ammonia-free products are used/highlighted, but does not state ALL treatments use them..
Removed "There are no hidden charges" — Fact states the price (3500 INR) is stated; absence of mention of hidden charges does not entail there are none..

Left out: Describes the treatment process (hair wash first, then treatment) to build trust and transparency. — a process claim needs a record that can establish "process", and the one(s) cited cannot.
Left out: Names the key service offered so readers know what to book. — a availability claim needs a record that can establish "policy", and the one(s) cited cannot.

Not on record: The name of the specific ammonia-free product brand or product line used, if the business wants to name it in the email.

Removed "The keratin treatment does not use ammonia-based products" — nothing on record can support a safety claim.

Not on record: A welcome email typically greets the reader by name or acknowledges their sign-up action — the business should record what trigger this email fires on (e.g., 'sent immediately after email sign-up on website') so the opening line can be written accurately.
Not on record: No brand name or business name is on record. The business should record their trading name so the email can be signed off correctly.
Not on record: No product image URL or visual asset reference is on record. The business should record a product photo URL if they want the email to include one.
